analysis.plain_explanation: An unauthorized transaction of Rs 12,000 was made on your credit card yesterday at an online store you have never used. Since you did not share any OTP, you have the right to report this fraudulent charge immediately to your bank and request a reversal. You should also report the incident on the national cyber crime portal to help authorities trace the fraud. Please note that banks require prompt reporting within specific windows to review liability, so you should act without delay. Keep in mind that we are providing legal information, not formal legal representation.

steps.title: Report financial fraud on the national cyber crime portal
steps.detail: Immediately register a complaint on the official cyber crime portal or call the helpline to report the unauthorized online transaction.

steps.title: Submit written dispute to your bank
steps.detail: Provide your call reference number along with a written fraud dispute form to your credit card issuer, requesting a full chargeback and reversal.
steps.where: Your credit card issuer / bank branch or customer support email

steps.title: Keep records of all correspondence
steps.detail: Preserve your SMS alerts, card statements, call logs, reference numbers, and any written replies from the bank for tracking liability.
steps.where: Safely stored on your phone or printed

plan.forum: Bank grievance cell and RBI Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (if the bank fails to resolve within the stipulated time)
plan.summary: Since you have already contacted your bank and obtained a call reference number, you should now file an official report on the cyber-crime portal using your SMS alert and statement details. Keep following up with your bank in writing to track your transaction dispute.

reasons: Scam and fraud cases need police and bank action that this tool can only guide you to. Get a lawyer if the police or bank refuse to act.
